info.title: Canvas Cloud API
info.summary: Collaborative canvases: REST, live Yjs rooms, accounts, linked apps and agent seams.
info.description: Every route of a Canvas Cloud server. All `/v1` routes speak JSON; errors are always `{"error": "<code>", "message": "…"}` (409 conflicts may carry extra fields). Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`: a session token (`cvs_…`), a personal access token (`cvt_…`; read-scoped tokens may only GET/HEAD and never join a live room — `403 read_only_token`), or a linked-app key (`cva_…`) plus `X-Canvas-User: <subject>` to act as one of the app's users (without that header an app key is accepted only on `/v1/apps/self/*`). WebSocket upgrades and `text/event-stream` GETs may pass the credential as `?token=` instead. In canvas routes `{id}` is a canvas UUID or the literal `personal` (the caller's Personal canvas, created on first use). A canvas the caller is not a member of is indistinguishable from one that does not exist (`404`). Agents can also use the MCP endpoint (`POST /mcp`) and the plain-text guide at `/llms.txt`.

get.summary: What this server is and offers
get.description: Public. Clients (and a web app probing its own origin) learn the server name, version, sign-in methods, web-app hosting, features and limits.
Your canvases: the Personal canvas first (created on first use), then most recently updated.

post.description: Creates a `shared` canvas owned by the caller. `name` is trimmed, control characters dropped, 1–200 characters.

patch.description: Owner only (`403` for editors); `400` on the Personal canvas. Also updates the document's `meta.name` (synced to connected peers).

delete.description: Owner only; `400` on the Personal canvas. Deletes members, invites, links, updates and mentions (cascade) and closes the room (sockets get close code `4404`); former members get a `deleted` event.

get.description: Owner first, then by join time. Any member may list.

delete.description: The owner removes anyone else; any member removes themselves (leave). The owner cannot leave (`400`). Removed users' sockets close with `4403`.

get.description: Any member; newest first.

post.description: Owner or editor; not on the Personal canvas (`400`). Inviting yourself is `400`, an existing member `409`. A new invite is `201`; an already-pending email is a re-send (`200`): when the invitee has an account and the last reminder is at least 30 s old, `nudged_at` is set and the invitee gets another `invited` event (`nudged: true`).

delete.description: The canvas owner or the member who sent it. The invitee (if they have an account) gets an `invite_revoked` event.

get.description: Pending invites addressed to your email (case-insensitive), newest first.

post.description: Only the invitee; anything else (wrong user, already used, declined, revoked, unknown) is `404`. Returns the canvas (your view, `role: editor`).

get.description: Owner only; tokens are never listed.

post.description: Any member; not on the Personal canvas. The body may be empty, `{}` or `{"role":"editor"}`. The token is shown only in this response; the web landing page is `/join/{token}`.

201.description: The new link and its token.

get.summary: Preview what a share link opens
get.description: Any signed-in user holding the token. Unknown, revoked or deleted-canvas tokens are `404 link_not_found`.

post.summary: Join a canvas through a share link
post.description: Idempotent: adds an editor membership when needed (never downgrades the owner), accepts the caller's pending invite to the canvas, increments `uses`, publishes `member_added`. Returns the canvas as `GET /v1/canvases` shows it.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket speaking the standard y-websocket protocol (sync step 1/2 and updates in lib0 v1 encoding, awareness). HTTP/2 extended CONNECT also works. Browsers pass `?token=`. Read-only tokens are refused (`403 read_only_token`). Messages ≤ 8 MiB. Close codes: `4403` removed from the canvas, `4404` canvas deleted, `1001` server shutting down, `1009` message too big. With the `y-websocket` client: `new WebsocketProvider("wss://host/v1/canvases", "<id>/ws", doc, {params: {token}})`.

get.summary: The Yjs document as one update

parameters.name: sv
parameters.description: Base64 Yjs state vector: return only what the caller is missing.

get.summary: The canvas in the agent read format
get.description: Shapes sorted top-to-bottom then left-to-right, live agents, the shape count and the last 50 chat messages. Text, titles and labels are cut to 500 characters unless `full=true`.

post.description: Applies up to 500 ops in order in one transaction, persisted and broadcast to the live room. A bad op is skipped and reported in `errors` (by index); the rest still apply. Envelope problems are `200` with `errors: [{index: -1, …}]`. Body ≤ 4 MiB. The body may also be a bare array of ops.

post.summary: Notify people mentioned in a chat message
post.description: Called by the client that sent a chat message. Members of the canvas among `user_ids` (other than the caller) are notified (`mention` event, listed by `GET /v1/mentions`); others are `skipped`. At most 100 targets; `message_id` ≤ 128 characters; `excerpt` cut to 200 characters (stored encrypted). Rate limit: 60 calls per minute per user (`429`).

get.description: Mentions of the caller on canvases they can still see, newest first, plus the total unread count.

post.description: Send `ids` (≤ 500), `canvas_id`, or both (`400` with neither). The caller's other clients get a `mention_read` event.

get.summary: Find people to invite or mention
get.description: Other enabled users whose display name or email contains `q` (all when empty).

post.description: Public. The first password account on an instance may always be created; after that the server's signup policy decides (`allow_signup`, optionally narrowed to `signup_domains`; `GET /v1/info` → `signup`). Passwords are 10–256 characters. Returns a session.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Public. Any failure is the same `401 invalid_credentials`.

post.summary: End this session (or all of them)
post.description: Session credentials only (`403 session_required`). `{"all": true}` ends every session of the user.

get.summary: Who you are and how you authenticated

post.description: Session credentials only. Ends every other session.

get.description: Public; for login buttons.
Public. Redirects to the identity provider (authorization code + PKCE + nonce). `redirect_uri` must be one of the provider's configured `redirect_uris` or same-origin with the server's `public_url`.
Public; the identity provider redirects here. Finds (or, when allowed, creates) the user by verified email, then redirects to the `redirect_uri` given to `start` with `#token=cvs_…` (or `#error=…`).
Session credentials only (`403 session_required`); live tokens, newest first; secrets are never listed.

limit.description: Most live tokens a user may have.

post.description: Session credentials only — a token cannot mint tokens. The `cvt_…` secret is in this response only. At most 50 live tokens (`403 token_limit`).

get.description: Any credential (`?token=` accepted, since EventSource cannot set headers). Frames: `event: canvas` with `id: <n>` and `data: {"type":"canvas","canvas_id","kind"}` (kind: created, renamed, deleted, update, invited, invite_revoked, invite_declined, member_added, member_removed, mention, mention_read); `event: ready` once after any replay; `event: resync` when the resume point is gone or the stream lagged — refetch, then carry on; `: keepalive` every 15 s. Resume with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?last_event_id=`).

put.summary: Create or update one of your app's users
put.description: A new user gets `id` when it is given, a UUID and free, else a new UUIDv7. When the email belongs to a user not linked to this app: with the app's `trust_email` the existing user is linked to this subject (id unchanged), else `409 email_taken`.

delete.summary: Delete or unlink one of your app's users
delete.description: A pure app user (no password, no other app link) is deleted with everything they own (their canvases are deleted, rooms closed with `4404`, members notified); otherwise the user is only unlinked from this app. Their sockets are disconnected either way.

post.description: At most 1000 users; each is its own transaction, so one bad row does not sink the batch. Results are in request order.

get.summary: Every canvas event of your app's users (Server-Sent Events)
get.description: Frames: `event: canvas`, `id: <n>`, `data: {"subject","user_id","canvas_id","kind"}`; `event: resync` with `data: {}` when the `Last-Event-ID` is no longer buffered; keepalive every 15 s.

get.summary: Canvases owned by your app's users

delete.summary: Delete a canvas owned by one of your users
delete.description: Closes the room (`4404`) and publishes `deleted` to its members.

get.summary: Content digest of a stored canvas
get.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON rendering of the stored document (reloaded from the database); equal for any complete set of the same updates. Used to verify imports.

post.description: Requires the app's `allow_import` (`403` otherwise). The body is NDJSON, one canvas, lines in this order: `canvas`, `member`…, `invite`…, `link`…, `mention`…, `update`…, `end` (see the `Import*Line` schemas). Lines ≤ 32 MiB; the body limit is `limits.import_max_bytes` in `GET /v1/info`. Every subject must already be provisioned (`422 unknown_subject`). Errors name the line: `422 bad_line`, `bad_update`, `count_mismatch`, `incomplete_history`. `mode=create` (default): an existing id is `409 canvas_exists` with the stored `digest`. `mode=replace`: only for a canvas this app imported earlier. A Personal canvas replaces the owner's empty one; a non-empty one is `409 personal_exists` unless `mode=replace`.

get.description: Public. `servers` is the server's configured public URL.

post.description: MCP Streamable HTTP: one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per POST; a request gets one `application/json` response, a notification `202`. Protocol `2025-06-18` (also `2025-03-26`, including its batches); stateless (no `Mcp-Session-Id`). Same credentials as the REST API; read-only tokens see only the read tools. A browser `Origin` must be in the server's CORS allow-list (or be `public_url`'s origin), else `403`. Methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Tools: whoami, list_canvases, create_canvas, rename_canvas, read_canvas, apply_ops, list_members, invite, create_share_link, list_mentions, mark_mentions_read. Other HTTP methods: `405` with `Allow: POST`.

400.description: Not a valid JSON-RPC message, a batch under 2025-06-18, or an unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version.

get.description: Public, `text/plain; charset=utf-8` (llmstxt.org shape): auth, MCP config, REST basics, ops cheat-sheet, live rooms, limits.
Public; never touches the database. With a web app configured (`web_app_url`, or `web_root`) a well-formed token redirects there; otherwise a plain "open this link in your canvas app" page.

bearer.description: A session (`cvs_…`, from login, signup or single sign-on) or a personal access token (`cvt_…`, from `POST /v1/tokens` or the /account page). Read-scoped tokens: GET/HEAD only. A linked-app key (`cva_…`) also goes here, with `X-Canvas-User` to act as one of the app's users.

appKey.description: A linked-app key (`cva_…`). Without `X-Canvas-User` it may call only `/v1/apps/self/*`.

canvasUser.name: X-Canvas-User
canvasUser.description: With an app key: the subject (the app's own user id) to act as; it must be provisioned via `PUT /v1/apps/self/users/{subject}` (`401 unknown_user` otherwise).

CanvasId.name: id
CanvasId.description: A canvas UUID, or `personal` for the caller's Personal canvas.

QueryToken.name: token
QueryToken.description: The credential, for WebSocket upgrades and `text/event-stream` requests that cannot send `Authorization`.

Subject.name: subject
Subject.description: The app's own id for the user.

NotFound.description: No such thing, or not visible to the caller (`not_found`, `link_not_found`, …).

Conflict.description: Conflict (`conflict`, `email_taken`, `canvas_exists` with `digest`, `personal_exists`, …); may carry extra fields.

Unprocessable.description: The import body is well-formed but invalid; `message` names the line (`bad_line`, `bad_update`, `unknown_subject`, `count_mismatch`, `incomplete_history`).

root.description: This server hosts a canvas web app at `/`.

features.description: e.g. canvases, mentions, share_links, people, accounts, access_tokens, events, oidc, apps, import, mcp.

invitee.description: The account with that email, when one exists.

token.description: Shown only here. Open `/join/{token}` or call `POST /v1/canvas-links/{token}/join`.

member.description: The caller is already a member.

Color.description: A palette name (yellow, pink, blue, green, purple, gray, white) or `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`.

Endpoint.description: An arrow end: a free point, or a reference to a shape (optionally pinned to a side).

Shape.description: One shape in the read format. Which optional fields appear depends on `type`.

by.description: Who created it (an agent name or a user).

src.description: Image source; `data:` URLs are described, not echoed.

tally.description: Picks per column, in column order.

frame.description: The innermost frame this shape sits in.

agents.description: Agents written to in the last 2 minutes.

ShapeInput.description: A shape to add. Omit `x` and `y` to auto-place it in free space near the request's `near`.

url.description: http, https, mailto (plus any configured extra schemes); bare hosts get https://.

Op.description: One edit. Ids may be written `shape:<id>`; later ops can refer to ids added earlier in the same request.

oneOf.description: Deletes every shape; refused unless the request has `confirm: true`.

as.description: The agent doing the edit: created shapes get `by` = name and its cursor shows in the room. A bare string is a name.

near.description: Where auto-placement looks for free space.

ids.description: Per op: the shape id it created or touched; null when it failed, and for clear.

index.description: Op index; -1 for a problem with the whole request.

expires_in_days.description: Omit for a token that never expires.

id.description: Preferred id for a new user (used when free).

ImportLine.description: One NDJSON line of import format v1.

token_sha256_hex.description: Digest of the token, so existing links keep working.

b64.description: A lib0 v1 Yjs update, in original order (a snapshot first, as an update).

JsonRpcMessage.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request (`id`, `method`, `params`), notification (no `id`) or response (`result` or `error`).
